In the United States, the AVMA Veterinary Clinical Trials Registry, AniTrial, and the Dog Aging Project connect pet owners with hundreds of active studies. Dog and cat owners there can access new cancer immunotherapy, longevity drugs like rapamycin, and novel treatments for kidney disease, epilepsy, and arthritis. In Australia, clinical research is fragmented across seven veterinary schools with no centralised, owner-accessible registry. Pet owners have no way to discover if a trial relevant to their pet's condition exists. They cannot enrol. Research teams struggle to recruit participants. PetTrials fixes that. For free. No centralised trial registry Unlike the US, which has the AVMA registry with hundreds of active studies, Australian pet owners have nowhere to search for trials. Research fragmented across 7 vet schools UQ, Sydney, Melbourne, Murdoch, CSU, JCU, and Adelaide each run independent studies with no shared recruitment platform.
